info.title: Git Bridge API
info.description:
Multi-provider git repository mirroring service.

Mirrors repositories between CodeCommit, GitLab and GitHub. Sync is event-driven: CodeCommit events arrive over SQS (not an HTTP endpoint), while GitLab and GitHub push events arrive on the webhook endpoints below. A manual retry endpoint re-runs a sync for a single repository.

All endpoints here are machine-facing and reachable on the public host. Webhook senders are configured in the respective providers; the retry endpoint is called by operators.

post.description:
Receives push events from GitLab and triggers a mirror sync for the matching repository.

The `project.path_with_namespace` field is matched against `target_path` or `source_path` in the repo configuration.

The sync runs in the background, so a 200 means the event was accepted — not that the mirror finished.

parameters.name: X-Gitlab-Token
parameters.description: Secret token for webhook verification. Required only when `WEBHOOK_GITLAB_SECRET` is configured.

200.description: Event accepted, mirror sync started asynchronously

post.description:
Receives push events from GitHub and triggers a mirror sync for the matching repository.

The `repository.full_name` field is matched against `target_path` or `source_path` in the repo configuration.

The sync runs in the background, so a 200 means the event was accepted — not that the mirror finished.

parameters.name: X-Hub-Signature-256
parameters.description: HMAC-SHA256 signature of the request body (`sha256=<hex>`). Required only when `WEBHOOK_GITHUB_SECRET` is configured.

200.description: Event accepted, mirror sync started asynchronously

post.description:
Re-runs the mirror for one repository, for use after a failed sync.

Authentication is a bearer token compared in constant time. When `RETRY_API_TOKEN` is empty the endpoint is disabled and every request gets 404 — the route stays registered so the response is uniform whether or not the feature is on.

The sync runs in a background goroutine, so a 200 means the request was **accepted**, not that the mirror succeeded — and not even that the repository exists. An unknown `repo`, or a direction the repository's own `direction` disallows, still returns 200 here and only fails inside the goroutine. Check the pod logs (`source=retry-api`) or the Slack notification for the outcome.

200.description: Retry accepted, mirror sync started asynchronously. Echoes back what was queued — this does not mean the repo exists or the sync will succeed.

400.description: Malformed JSON, missing `repo`, or a `direction` outside the allowed values. An unknown repo is NOT rejected here — see the 200 description.

401.description: Missing, malformed, or incorrect bearer token

path_with_namespace.description: Full project path used for repo matching

full_name.description: Full repository name used for repo matching

repo.description: Repository name as declared under `repos[].name` in the config.

direction.description:
Mirror direction to run. Defaults to `auto` when omitted or empty. Matching is case-insensitive.

`auto` resolves in this order: the repository's explicit `retry_direction` if set, otherwise a built-in fallback by the repository's `direction` (bidirectional resolves to target-to-source; one-way repositories resolve to their single allowed direction).

ref.description: Optional single ref to sync. Omit to sync every ref.

source.description: Optional caller identity, recorded as the event's trigger. Only `cron` is accepted — the reconcile CronJob sets it so its scheduled calls are distinguishable from a hand-run retry, which is recorded as `retry-api`. Any other value is rejected with 400, keeping the trigger vocabulary closed.

dest.description: The destination tip being overwritten. Required with `force`, and becomes the push's lease — without it the force would run against whatever the destination holds when the push finally executes, which after a minute-long fetch is not necessarily the commit the caller decided about. A force with no `dest` returns 400.

force.description:
Apply a rewind the push guard would otherwise withhold.

The mirror refuses a push that would move a ref backwards at the destination — the destination already contains what this side holds, so the write would discard commits there rather than mirror them. That refusal also catches a rewind somebody meant to make, and this flag is how they say which it is.

It does NOT skip the lease: the push still carries the destination tip it was checked against, so a commit arriving between the check and the write is still refused. Three limits keep it narrow — `ref` is required, so one call moves at most one ref; `dest` is required, so it can only discard the commit the caller looked at; and `source: cron` is refused, so the unattended reconcile can never carry a bypass. All three violations return 400.

actor.description: Optional attribution recorded on the history event and included in the Slack message. The console button fills it from the portal's `X-Auth-User`.

RetryAccepted.description: Echo of the queued retry. Returned before the sync runs.

direction.description: The direction as received — `auto` is echoed literally, not the resolved value.

ref.description: Empty when no ref was requested.

CodeCommitEvent.description: EventBridge event consumed via SQS (not an HTTP endpoint)
